scenario: WIBTA if I told my cousin his kid can’t stay in our house? | My cousin (M27) recently moved in with my husband and I. We completely closed of the very large main bedroom and bathroom to create a flatlet for him that’s separate from the house with his own entrance so it’s basically two separate units of one house. Now my cousin has a 2 year old and he’s busy with a custody battle with his ex so he can get to spend more time with his son. I completely support this and really hopes he gets more time with his son. Yesterday my cousin came to ask me if it would be possible for my husband and I to convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son if and when he comes to visit over weekends. There is no access from my cousin’s room into our part of the house and he doesn’t have keys to come and go as he pleases. I understand that the court will be looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son to stay with him (and to be honest his current room and bathroom is more than big enough) but I’m not comfortable with letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin has no access to him and I’m not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that’s just the way my family is and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. WIBTA for telling him I will not allow his son to sleep in our house and completely jeopardizing his court case?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my cousin that his kid can't stay in our house. Let me break this down step by step. First, my cousin moved in with my husband and me. We converted the main bedroom and bathroom into a separate flatlet for him, so he has his own entrance. That means our living spaces are completely separate. He doesn't have access to our part of the house, and he doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. Now, my cousin has a 2-year-old, and he's in the middle of a custody battle with his ex. He wants to spend more time with his son, and I fully support that. I really hope he gets more time with his son. Yesterday, he asked if we could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son when he comes over weekends. I understand that the court is looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son. His current room and bathroom are more than big enough, so I don't think the court would have an issue with that. But I'm not comfortable letting his son sleep in our house because my cousin doesn't have access to him. I don't want to take responsibility for his kid, especially since he can't come and go as he wants. The whole family is involved in this because that's just how my family is. Everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his custody situation to get him more time with his son. But I'm wondering if I'm being unreasonable by saying no. Would it be wrong to tell him I won't allow his son to stay in our house, potentially jeopardizing his court case? On one hand, I'm respecting my cousin's situation and trying to support him. On the other hand, I have boundaries about my own space and not wanting to take on the responsibility of his child. I'm also concerned about the legal implications if something were to happen while the child is in our house. I need to consider the court's perspective. They're looking at whether my cousin has a suitable living arrangement. If he can't have his son stay with him because of our refusal, that might make it look like he doesn't have the necessary space, which could hurt his custody case. But I also have to think about my own comfort and safety. Maybe I should communicate my concerns clearly to my cousin. Let him know that I support him but that I'm not comfortable having his son in our space. Perhaps we can find a compromise, like having the child stay in his flatlet when he's here, or maybe he can use another family member's place. I also need to think about the family dynamics. Everyone expects me to help, but I have to prioritize my own boundaries. It's important to stand up for myself while still being supportive in other ways. In the end, I have to decide whether my refusal is reasonable or if it's putting my cousin at a disadvantage. If I say no, am I being selfish, or am I protecting my own space and responsibilities? It's a tough call, but I think I need to stick to my boundaries while offering alternative solutions to help my cousin.
